## /rebar-debug FINAL REPORT — e4a6-545b-36af-456d (baldish-regainable-steed)

**PROBLEM.** `_cas_backoff` slept between the merge and the next push without re-fetching, so
each retry re-pushed state captured BEFORE the sleep (staler, not fresher), and the fixed
unjittered schedule `(0.25, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0)` made colliding writers wake in lockstep and
re-collide.

**PROVEN ROOT CAUSE (one defect, two symptoms).**
1. STALENESS — `_cas_backoff(attempt, sleep_fn)` was called AFTER `_merge_remote_under_lock`
   inside `_recover_non_fast_forward` (`if recovered:` block). The push loop
   (`push_tickets_branch`, push.py) then re-pushes on the NEXT iteration with no intervening
   fetch, so the sleep never buys a fresher base — the retry pushes pre-sleep state.
2. LOCKSTEP — `_CAS_BACKOFF_SECONDS` is a deterministic tuple with no jitter, so two writers
   that collide once sleep identical durations, wake together, and re-collide.

**PROOF.** Runtime instrumentation of the real recovery path (fake git recording arg vectors +
a `sleep_fn` capturing delays) produced, under seeded contention:
`push(fail) -> fetch -> merge -> SLEEP(0.25) -> push(fail) -> fetch -> merge -> SLEEP(0.5) -> push(ok)`.
The op immediately AFTER every SLEEP was `push`, never `fetch` — the staleness mechanism,
observed at runtime, not inferred. Jitter proof: 200 samples of the base delay were byte-for-byte
identical (all 0.25) pre-fix.

**DEFECT ORIGIN + caused_by.** Introduced by commit `d2e96326a20f` (ticket
`ebee-e959-8015-4e02`, "Stop reading a GitHub 500 as a stolen ref lease"), which ADDED the
`_cas_backoff` call to achieve CAS convergence but placed it after the merge and left it
unjittered — an incomplete implementation of the intended convergence backoff. The mechanism
did not exist before ebee (date test: implicated lines and the good->bad transition coincide),
so this is DIRECT attribution. Recorded: `link e4a6 -> ebee caused_by`. Close class =
`plan_defect` (the originating plan specified backoff AFTER each recovery — the wrong placement).

**RED -> GREEN TEST.** New held-out oracle `tests/unit/test_cas_backoff_refetch_baldish.py` (5
tests): ordering (SLEEP precedes re-fetch on every retry), jitter (200 samples vary), escalation
preserved under jitter, zero-contention negative control, and AC4/B4 best-effort-exhaustion
does-not-raise. Confirmed RED for the right reason pre-fix (after-backoff next op was `push`;
all jitter samples identical). Mutation teeth: restoring the original placement -> ordering test
RED; removing jitter -> jitter test RED. GREEN post-fix (5/5).

**FIX (34 changed src lines, 2 files).**
- `push_recovery.py`: moved `_cas_backoff(attempt, sleep_fn)` to the TOP of
  `_recover_non_fast_forward` (order: SLEEP -> fetch -> merge), removing the post-merge
  `if recovered:` block. The caller's next push now follows a merge of freshly-fetched state.
- `push_classify.py`: added additive jitter — `delay = base * (1.0 + random.random() *
  _CAS_BACKOFF_JITTER)` with `_CAS_BACKOFF_JITTER = 0.25`, landing in `[base, 1.25*base]`.
  Always >= base and bounded below the next base (2x ratio), so escalation is preserved.
  `random` is stdlib (already used repo-wide); no new dependency. Mirrors the established
  additive-jitter idiom in `_engine/.../jira_datacenter/retry.py`. B4 best-effort delivery
  contract preserved (exhaustion returns without raising).

**SCOPE & SAFETY.** Caller-dependency gate PASSED — `_cas_backoff` has one caller
(`_recover_non_fast_forward`), itself called only by the `push_tickets_branch` wrapper; blast
radius fully internal to `_store`. No public contract, signature, or dependency change. Two
pre-existing timing tests in `test_push_strict.py` were STRENGTHENED (not weakened) to encode
the reorder + jitter window. lint PASS, typecheck PASS (684 files), 39 push/recovery/fetch tests
pass.

**SIBLINGS (Step-7 sweep).** One confirmed construct/parity sibling filed and linked
`discovered_from`: `paediatric-orchestral-anemone (ad7b-6928-49fe-475a)` —
`last_pass.py`'s 3-attempt CAS publication loop uses an unjittered fixed `(0.1, 0.2)` schedule
(same lockstep class; its staleness half is already correct because it re-reads `old_oid` after
the sleep). Not folded into this bugfix: different subsystem/concurrency model, warrants its own
review. Recorded non-siblings: `_TRANSPORT_BACKOFF_SECONDS` (transient-TLS ride-out, not writer
contention — jitter N/A) and `_coordinated_fetch`'s `_FETCH_CAS_BACKOFF_S` (re-fetches after the
sleep and serializes rebar peers behind `fetch_coordination_lock`, so rebar-peer lockstep is
already prevented). Other `_cas_advance` callers (renew/steal/gate/pause) are single-shot
(surface the conflict, no retry loop) — not siblings.

**RESIDUAL RISK.** Low. The reorder adds a backoff on the fetch-failure/terminal paths that
previously slept only on success; this is a negligible, arguably-correct pre-retry backoff and
does not change the delivery contract (B4 verified). Jitter is bounded `[base, 1.25*base]`, so
worst-case latency grows <=25% while escalation ordering is retained.

**REPLICATION.** The original report ("sleeps between merge and push without re-fetching") no
longer reproduces: the ordering oracle now observes `... SLEEP -> fetch -> merge -> push ...`
on every retry (SLEEP precedes the re-fetch), and jitter samples vary.
